title: Access management: service accounts, API keys, and audit log UX notes
content:
Context and goal:

This doc captures UX notes and wireframe-level ideas for the org/team Access area in the Redwood Console: Members & Roles (RBAC), Service Accounts & API keys, and Audit Log views. Goal is to unify common admin workflows so that engineers and security teams can: create & rotate non-human credentials, audit activity, and manage RBAC at org and team scope with minimal cognitive overhead.

Constraints to keep in mind:
- Console must not reveal raw secrets after creation (only show API key once)
- Many customers run with nested teams/orgs and expect role inheritance semantics
- Private deploy customers may have different KMS integrations -> keep KMS UI details out of core flows (link to infra docs)
- Audit logs must be filterable and exportable; must surface sensitive events (key creation, role grant, login/fallback)

Personas and primary jobs-to-be-done:
- Platform Engineer (SRE): rotate service account keys, ensure least privilege, audit role changes
- Product Engineer: create short-lived API key for CI test harness, see usage after the fact
- Security Admin: investigate suspicious actions using audit logs and export evidence for compliance

High-level navigation and IA
- Top-level nav item: Access (icon: shield)
- First-level tabs inside Access: Members & Roles | Service Accounts | API Keys | Audit Logs | Token Usage (future)
- Contextual scope switcher (top-left): Org / Team dropdown with breadcrumbs. When viewing a Team scope, show inherited roles and an explicit "inherited from org" tag.

Wireframe notes (centered layout):
- Left column (30%): Scope & quick actions
  - Scope selector (Org / Team) + search teams
  - Quick actions: "Invite member", "Create service account", "Create API key" (primary)
  - Recent audit highlights (last 24h) small list with severity flags

- Center column (55%): Main list / table for selected tab
  - Members & Roles: table columns: Name | Email | Role(s) | Teams | Last active | Actions (edit, impersonate, remove)
    - Inline editing for roles: click role chip -> role picker modal -> save
    - Role change modal: show exact perms delta and example API calls that would be affected (helpful for engineers)
  - Service Accounts: table columns: Name | ID | Owner | Role(s) | Keys active | Last key rotated | Actions (new key, deactivate, delete)
    - Row action "New key" opens a stepper modal: 1) select expiration (1d/7d/30d/custom) 2) select scope (org/team) 3) generate -> show secret once + copy button + download .env file
    - Show warning microcopy when creating keys with long lifetimes: "Long-lived keys increase blast radius. Consider short-lived keys + token exchange."
  - API Keys (non-service-account): separate section for user-scoped keys and app-scoped keys (legacy). Same table patterns as service accounts keys.
  - Audit Logs: dense table with columns: Timestamp | Actor | Action | Target resource | Result (success/failure) | Context (IP, region) | Actions (view details)
    - Row expand reveals full JSON payload (redact PII by default), and quick link to orchestration tickets if present.

Right column (15%): Details & contextual help
  - When a row is selected show: full metadata, last 10 actions for that principal, recommended next steps (rotate key, restrict role, enable MFA), and links to docs.

Microcopy and interaction details
- Create service account dialog title: "Create service account"
  - Fields: Display name, Description, Assign role(s) (required), Team (optional), TTL for initial key (optional)
  - Primary CTA: "Create and generate key"
  - Post-creation toast: "Service account created. API key shown only once — store it securely." + CTA: "Download key (recommended)"
- Key display: large monospace box with copy button, small eye icon toggles reveal during creation flow only. After modal closed, key is gone.
- Revoke key: immediate action with 2-step confirmation (type service account ID to confirm for high risk actions)
- Role assignment UX: provide common role presets (Admin, Viewer, Inference-Invoker, Billing-Viewer) and suggest least-privilege recommendation with an inline "why" tooltip.

Audit log filtering and search
- Primary filters: time range (preset + custom), actor (email/service account), action type (create, delete, update, auth-failure), resource type (service_account, key, role, model), region/IP
- Text search over full payload (supports quoted phrases)
- Saved filters: allow saving and pinning a filter to the Access dashboard (team/shared filter with optional retention)
- Export options: CSV (all columns), JSON (full payload); for exports, default redaction on PII with checkbox to include raw payload (requires elevated permission)
- Pagination: cursor-based with link to jump to absolute time (useful for compliance investigations)

Error states and edge cases
- Key creation race: if two engineers click "New key" in parallel for the same service account, show second flow a banner: "A new key was created Xs ago — verify you are not reusing keys. Consider rotating older keys."
- Inherited role edit: if user attempts to modify an inherited role at a child-team scope, modal explains: "You cannot edit roles inherited from Org. Edit at Org scope or remove inheritance." CTA: "Open org settings"
- Large org scale: for orgs >10k members, default to server-side filtering and async exports. In UI show progress indicator and notify via console notification when export completes.

Accessibility and keyboard flows
- All modals trap focus and use ARIA labels for role chips and confirm inputs
- Keyboard shortcuts (global when Access tab open):
  - / -> focus search
  - N -> New service account
  - K -> New API key
  - G then A -> Go to Audit logs
- Screen reader note: when API key is generated, read "API key generated. Copy now. Warning: the key will not be displayed again."

Telemetry and metrics to validate UX decisions
- Conversion funnel: create-service-account -> key-generated -> key-copied -> used to call API (link usage back to token usage metrics)
- Time-to-rotate: track average days between creation and rotation per customer
- Audit search elasticity: measure frequency of saved filters and exports (if many downloads then maybe add scheduled exports)

Backlog / grooming items (priority ordered)
- JIRA-9834: Service account key creation modal + single-view key display (AC: secret visible once; copy + download; TTL selection; audit event emitted) [P0]
- JIRA-9841: Audit log saved filters + export job (AC: save filter, run export, notify user, role-gated) [P0]
- JIRA-9872: Role inheritance UI + edit guard for inherited roles (AC: show origin, block edits, link to origin) [P1]
- JIRA-9905: Key rotation wizard (bulk rotate + staggered rollout plan) (AC: staged rotation, health checks) [P1]
- JIRA-9920: Short-lived key template + built-in examples for CI (AC: 1d/7d presets, sample curl snippet) [P2]
- JIRA-9955: Audit log JSON detail viewer (redaction toggle gated by permission) [P2]

Acceptance criteria (example for JIRA-9834)
- Modal produces exactly one API secret string that is displayed once and copyable
- Secret cannot be retrieved after modal closes via UI
- Audit event "service_account.key.create" emitted with actor, service_account_id, key_id, expiration
- Unit + e2e tests validate copy button behavior and download flow

Open questions (to resolve in next sync)
- Should we support long-term personal API keys in first pass or require service accounts for all programmatic access?
- Do we surface KMS key ids for customers with Private deploys (some want KMS visibility in console)?
- What RBAC roles map to the redaction toggle for audit exports? Define policy (security team input needed).

Next steps / immediate deliverables
- Quick whiteboard session to sketch final modal flows (Asha + Diego + Priya) – schedule this week
- Design mockups for the Service Account flow + Audit filters (deliverable: three high-fidelity screens)
- Backend contract doc (fields emitted in audit events) to be drafted by eng-applied-ml + infra teams and linked from the PR

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working doc. I'm prioritizing low-friction flows for engineers while balancing compliance needs. Please add comments inline or slack me with strong preferences on TTL defaults and role presets.

Sample microcopy snippets (copy-ready):
- "Create API key" button: "Create API key (shown once)"
- Key warning: "This credential will be shown only once. Copy or download it now."
- Audit row failure badge: "Auth failure — check key status or token expiry"

End of notes.
